request.deadline: 12 months after deployment; month-6 yield distribution; monthly reporting; wind-down reconciliation within 30 days if triggered
deliverables: Deploy treasury-owned capital as USDM-denominated liquidity for Strike Finance V2
Return realized yield from the first six months to the Cardano Treasury at month 6
Return 100% of treasury-owned deployed assets, including remaining principal and realized yield, to the Cardano Treasury at month 12, minus any realized losses in wind-down scenarios

Provide monthly public transparency reports covering deployment status, utilization, volume, open interest, P&L, yield, drawdown, stablecoin exposure, market quality, distributions, and material risks
Provide third-party assurance reports at deployment confirmation, month-6 distribution, and month-12 return
request.recipient: independent council composed of Rami from Snek, Phil from Surf, and James from Monetra/Moneta as administrator and multisig overseer; exact treasury receiving account not stated in document
request.what: 12-month productive treasury deployment into Strike Finance V2 liquidity infrastructure, with ADA sold for USDM stablecoin liquidity and returned after the deployment period.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 9,000,000 ADA for a 12-month liquidity deployment into Strike Finance V2 rather than grant funding.
The deployed ADA will be sold for USDM, modeled at ADA = 0.15 USD to produce approximately 1,350,000 USDM of stablecoin liquidity.

Under modeled assumptions of a 10% USD-denominated annual percentage rate, the deployment is expected to generate approximately 135,000 USD or 900,000 ADA-equivalent in annual yield, but returns are not guaranteed.

Strike claims it has processed more than 1.13 billion USD in cumulative volume, facilitated roughly 968,000 to 1,001,000 trades, served more than 3,000 unique traders, generated over 1.16 million USD in protocol revenue, and produced over 3.25 million USD in liquidity-provider profit.
The document claims Strike represented over 50% of Cardano trading activity during the past six months.
The proposal states that operational custody will be handled by an independent multisig council and that Strike Finance will not have unilateral custody or control of treasury assets.
The document identifies major risks including ADA price appreciation risk, USDM depeg or redemption risk, smart contract risk, yield underperformance, custody risk, and operational multisig risk.

Governance review is triggered if drawdown exceeds 8%, reporting is missed for two consecutive monthly cycles, or unresolved custody, accounting, stablecoin, redemption, or smart contract concerns arise, with mandatory review at 10% drawdown and separate wind-down review above 20% drawdown.
Strike V2 is described as live on mainnet with public performance history, unofficial reviews, and an official audit by Christian Schmitz expected to be finalized by July 1, 2026.
The proposal targets 1,000,000,000 USD in 30-day volume, 5,000 traders, and a 5,000,000 USD annualized revenue run rate within 12 months.

summary: The document asks for a 9,000,000 ADA, 12-month treasury-owned liquidity deployment into Strike Finance V2, administered by an independent multisig council, with modeled yield, reporting, risk triggers, and return of funds, while relying heavily on proposer-stated adoption and performance metrics.
